entry_conditions: Observed support begins at index 0 with the Panda near the home posture, qpos arm approximately [0, -0.3, 0, -2.1, 0, 1.8, 0.785] rad, fingers open at about 0.04 m each, TCP near [-0.384, 0.0, 0.442] m, red_pose in the lower initial/blue-goal area around x -0.36 to -0.34, y -0.21 to -0.19, z 0.02 m, and blue_pose in the upper red-goal area. The model also covers later entry inside the expanded slice when causal observations show the red block already grasped/lifted or already released at the buffer and the robot remains in the demonstrated top-down corridor.
exit_conditions: A useful exit for the next skill is red_pose resting near the central buffer, approximately [-0.181, 0.0, 0.02] m, with the gripper open or reopening and blue_pose still near its upper marked region. By the late handoff boundary near index 460, demonstrated states have the TCP low over the blue block at about z 0.02-0.03 m and qpos[7:9] near 0.018 m as gripper closure on blue begins. Handoff may also occur earlier in the overlap near index 320 when the red block is buffered, fingers are open, and the TCP is high around z 0.29-0.30 m in the approach corridor to blue.
overlap_role: This policy intentionally learns the full shared transition [320, 460): red has been released, the gripper is open, the TCP retreats upward from the buffer, moves toward the blue block, descends over blue, and starts closing. This overlap allows the inference agent to transfer control either from a high open approach state or from a low blue-contact state without requiring an instantaneous discrete switch at red release.
successor_readiness: The successor should receive observations in which red_pose is stationary at the central buffer, blue_pose remains in the upper region, and the TCP/object relation to blue is within the demonstrated corridor: either high above/near the path to blue with open fingers, or centered over blue with low z and fingers closing. The relevant causal cues are tcp_pose minus blue_pose, red_pose minus the buffer point, qpos finger width, qvel, and whether blue_pose has not moved prematurely.
failure_signatures: Possible failure is indicated if the red block does not rise with the TCP after the grasp command, red_pose is not near the buffer after the lower/release portion, the gripper remains wide while the action should be carrying red, blue_pose moves before the intended blue handoff phase, or tcp_pose approaches blue with a large lateral error relative to blue_pose. These are observational warning signs of a missed pinch, dropped red block, premature blue contact, or leaving the demonstrated approach corridor; the learned policy does not include a guaranteed recovery controller.
continuation_guidance: Continue this policy during approach, red pinch/lift, carry to the buffer, lowering, release, retreat, and blue approach when causal observations match one of those phases. In particular, continue through red-buffer geometric success if the gripper is still opening or the TCP has not yet reached a successor-ready blue approach state; a single red-at-buffer cue alone may be too early for smooth transfer. Switch to the blue-to-goal successor once the red block is buffered and the TCP/finger state is clearly within the measured high-open or low-closing blue acquisition corridor.
limitations: These handoff conditions summarize measured successful demonstrations and the API-authored heuristic; they are not hard proof of contact or universal thresholds. The model observes only state vectors, not images, and it does not enforce IK, collision constraints, or object containment beyond what is learned from data. Robustness to large initial block offsets, failed closures, moved goals, clutter, or off-corridor recovery was not demonstrated.
